newsitem.title: JAPAN: Malaysia economic fundamentals strong - Anwar.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia economic fundamentals strong - Anwar.

text.p: Malaysia's Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Tuesday the country's economic fundamentals were strong despite some recent concerns about money market liquidity and credit curbs.

He told Reuters Financial Television in an interview that recent negative reactions in Malaysia's financial markets was a reaction to increase in U.S. interest rates and property market problems in the region.

"But, in the final analysis, what is important in an economy is fundamentals, and our fundamentals fortunately remain very strong," Anwar said. He is in Fukuoka to attend the annual meeting of the Asian Development Bank (ADB).
Malaysia imposed fresh curbs on lending to the property sector and for share purchases in March to prevent what it said was unnecessary speculation in the sectors.
Around the same time, asset inflation problems emerged in Thailand, the Philippines and, a little earlier, in Singapore.
"These measures (credit curbs) are necessary and critical in managing the economy," he told RFTV.

"There is a transient reaction, quite negative, adverse, in the financial community, partly due to the development of interest rates in the United States (and) jittery reaction to developments in the region," he said.
